name: Fred Perry
why: The laurel-wreath piqué shirt from 1952, still made in Leicester; the mod and the terrace wardrobe since, Japanese-owned, with no US store of its own since Broome Street closed.
origin: Founded in 1952 in London, England (brand story places the founding meeting in a South London restaurant) by Fred Perry and Tibby Wegner.

notes.tech: Thread proposed 1 (2026-10-10): RWS (Responsible Wool Standard) merino and lambswool; recycled polyester and recycled polyamide; polyamide Taslan (texturised nylon) on padded jackets; no named membrane — NONE: no licensed membrane, insulation or performance fibre named on any of 223 men's clothing PDPs (RWS and recycled fibres are sourcing standards, not tech); share of range 0 of 223 styles name an owned or licensed technology; 54 of 223 are synthetic-le. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.
notes.craft: Thread proposed 3 (2026-10-10): Fred Perry owns no factory (its Modern Slavery Statement lists 35 supplier factories in six countries) but names its Leicester makers, UK Piqué and ESP, for the Made in England shirts and documents their process (5-4-4 tipping, hand draw-threading). That naming covers about 9 of 223 men's styles; the rest of the range states neither maker nor country, so a 3 rests on the Made in England line alone Seated as proposed, pending ruling.

cities: No store of its own in the US · department stores, independent shops, and its own site

marks: RWS (Responsible Wool Standard) merino and lambswool
polyamide Taslan (texturised nylon) on padded jackets

craft_evidence.owned: no evidence: Modern Slavery Statement (FY2024, signed Richard Gilmore, MD) says 35 live factories in UK, China, Vietnam, Portugal, Germany, Thailand, majority sourced direct from the manufacturer; no factory claimed as owned
craft_evidence.makers: partly, off-PDP: brand article (Feb 2021) names UK Piqué (knitting) and ESP (garment making), Leicester, as makers of the Made in England M2, M3, M12 shirts; PDPs name no maker
craft_evidence.mills: no: no cloth or yarn mill named on PDPs; only fibre standards (RWS wool, Better Cotton membership in footer)
craft_evidence.madein: 13 of 223 men's clothing PDPs state a country (9 Made in England line styles incl. bullets/collection, 4 Made in Portugal); the other 210 state none (all 223 read 10 Oct)
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: 1952 tennis shirts; founded by Fred Perry (triple Wimbledon champion) with Tibby Wegner after a late-1940s meeting in a South London restaurant; Made in England shirts knitted and cut in Leicester
craft_evidence.process: partial: Made in England article documents 5-4-4 tipping knitted on the oldest machine Fred Perry uses, collars and cuffs draw-threaded by hand, piqué knitted, dyed, cut, embroidered and hand-finished in Leicester; main range PDPs give only fabric and fit bullets
craft_evidence.reasoning: Fred Perry owns no factory (its Modern Slavery Statement lists 35 supplier factories in six countries) but names its Leicester makers, UK Piqué and ESP, for the Made in England shirts and documents their process (5-4-4 tipping, hand draw-threading). That naming covers about 9 of 223 men's styles; the rest of the range states neither maker nor country, so a 3 rests on the Made in England line alone and could be argued down to 2.

ownership.owner: Hit Union Co., Ltd. (Japan), owner since 1995 per FashionNetwork (2 Jan 2018); UK operating company Fred Perry Limited (03114528) is 75%+ controlled by Fred Perry (Holdings) Limited per Companies House PSC register

opview: “…my name is better known worldwide, not for winning Wimbledon three times, but because of Fred Perry shirts and sportswear.” — Fred Perry, founder, Fred Perry Subculture, "The Sweatband" (brand journal, quoting Fred Perry)
